534.t: Futures for graduates and being versatile
534.s: He tells of students touring with pop and jazz acts, urges versatility, and cites Joshua Redman as the rare exception who makes a living only playing jazz.
534.q: Well that’s the million dollar question. I’m glad I teach in L.A., in Los Angeles, because I think there’s a lot of opportunity for my students and I’ve got a brilliant jazz piano student who got his master’s degree who is touring with Christina Aguilera right now, and another brilliant jazz piano…

554.t: Future of jazz students and work
554.s: Whether young jazz players will find places to practice and work.
554.q: Yeah, I’m not sure whether there’s going to be enough work although they say the cream will rise to the top if there’s some outstanding musicians I guess somebody’ll say this guy’s too good like to — you know, you have to discover them.

1012.t: Jazz education and the need to be versatile
1012.s: Graduates must play many styles, write, and take gigs like weddings; only a tiny fraction become stars.
1012.q: I think you said it best when you said when we were talking before, you said, this: you’ve got to be versatile. See the days for me, if I could go out and play post-bop like Joe Henderson and those guys, that’s the music that I really love. You’re not going to eat on that. You’ve got to find a way…

414.t: Advice for students and jazz education
414.s: Opportunities are harder than before, though jazz is now taught in colleges and the service bands are strong.
414.q: Well, there’s always a way if you’re, if you want it badly enough, you’re going to get it. It’s probably more difficult now than it was when we were younger.

1047.t: Rising in opera versus jazz, and voice types in conservatories
1047.s: Success depends on opportunity and dedication; conservatory scholarships favor scarcer male voices.
1047.q: You know, it depends. It just depends on your opportunities, it depends on your dedication, it depends on your voice. I don’t mean like how good or bad you are, I mean like a soprano’s chances are not as easy as a bass baritone for instance. Just getting into a

685.t: Teaching young players and what hurts jazz today
685.s: Peterson tells students at York University to listen to the greats and complains that money and agents distract them.
685.q: He was, yes. I’m thankful that I was fortunate enough to have been reared in that era, even though I was a bystander, I was a listener at the outset of it, and was fortunate enough to be able to hear all of these greats and learn from them. And that’s the thing that I tell, I teach at York…

216.t: Options for graduating jazz musicians and Girl from Ipanema
216.s: Ricker says having many skills gives options, most jazz players teach, and the two joke about Girl from Ipanema requests.
216.q: Yeah. Well they weren’t great 20 or 30 years ago either. You know the thing I think is that if you’ve got many different things that you can do, and do at a high level, you can have more options, and that’s the name of the game, you know, having some options. And jazz people, I mean I’d say 95…

722.s: He says prospects are poor but passion and entrepreneurial skills, such as Eastman's Arts Leadership Program, help.
722.q: Not too good, to be honest. And I think about that. Because I think not only in music but even say you have a degree in painting. Where are you going to go? You know, you have a degree in poetry. What are you going to do? You know, Starbucks? Hey. But I do believe that with passion and commitment…

472.t: Versatility for young players: Tia Fuller with Beyonce
472.s: Heath agrees young musicians must be flexible and cites his student Tia Fuller.
472.q: They do. I have a student now, she’s a great saxophonist, and she’s playing with Beyonce. She’s been with Beyonce, Tia Fuller, her name is. [She’s a] great saxophonist. I met her when I went to Spellman College, and then she left Spellman and went to somewhere in Colorado to another college. She…

413.t: Advising students to join the Navy
413.s: Too many schools turn out too many musicians.
413.q: It got too complicated for me. So as far as a future in musicianship, with all these schools turning people around -- I don't know if I told this or not in one of the earlier times, but in case I did I'll make it fairly short.
